topic.name: Factoring Perfect Square Trinomials With Leading Coefficients

question.explanation:
The "square of a difference" formula states that

\[ a^2 - {\color{red}{2}}a{\color{blue}{b}} + {\color{blue}b}^2 = (a-{\color{blue}{b}})^2 . \]

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

\[ 9x^2-12x+4. \]

First, we write both the quadratic term and the constant term as perfect squares: \begin{align} (3x)^2 - 12x + ({\color{blue}{2}})^2 \end{align}

Next, we factor a $2$ out of the linear term: \begin{align} (3x)^2 - {\color{red}{2}}(6x) + ({\color{blue}{2}})^2 \end{align}

Then, we write the middle parentheses $(6x)$ as a product of $3x$ and ${\color{blue}2}\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} (3x)^2 - {\color{red}{2}}(3x \cdot {\color{blue}{2}} ) + ({\color{blue}{2}})^2 \end{align}

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of difference formula with $a=3x$ and ${\color{blue}{b}} = {\color{blue}{2}}.$ This gives \begin{align} (3x - {\color{blue}{2}})^2. \end{align}

example.title: Factoring a Perfect Square Trinomial Generated by the Square of a Difference

question.explanation:
Notice that the leading coefficient is negative. To reduce the expression to a more familiar form, we can factor out $-1,$ as follows:

\begin{align} -9x^2+4x-\dfrac{4}{9} &= \\[3pt] - \left( 9x^2-4x+\dfrac{4}{9} \right) \end{align}

Now, we factor the quadratic expression inside the parentheses using the square of a difference formula:

\begin{align*} 9x^2-4x+\dfrac{4}{9} &= \\[3pt] (3x)^2-4x+\left( \dfrac{2}{3}\right)^2 &= \\[3pt] (3x)^2 -2 \cdot \left( \dfrac{2}{3}\cdot 3x\right ) + \left( \dfrac{2}{3}\right)^2 &= \\[3pt] \left(3x - \dfrac{2}{3} \right)^2& \end{align*}

Therefore, our original expression factors as follows:

\begin{align*} - \left( 9x^2-4x+\dfrac{4}{9} \right) &= \\[3pt] - \left(3x - \dfrac{2}{3} \right)^2& \end{align*}

example.title: Factoring a Perfect Square Trinomial With a Negative Leading Coefficient

question.explanation:
Notice that all of the terms have a common factor of $4.$ Therefore, we can simplify the expression by factoring out $4,$ as follows: \begin{align*} 16r^2 - 16r + 4 &=\\[3pt] 4(4r^2 - 4r + 1) \end{align*}

Now, let's factor the expression inside parentheses using the square of a difference formula: \begin{align} 4r^2 - 4r + 1 &=\\[3pt] (2r)^2 - 4r +1^2 &=\\[3pt] (2r)^2 - 2 \cdot (2r \cdot 1) + 1^2 &=\\[3pt] (2r - 1)^2 \end{align}

Therefore, our original expression factors as follows: \begin{align*} 4(4r^2 - 4r + 1) &=\\[3pt] 4(2r - 1)^2 \end{align*}
